summary: The query must emit every one of the cubic number of three-topping combinations and return them in value order, so output generation and ordering already match the self-join-and-sort method's principal work.

optimality.argument: There are K distinct required rows and arbitrary decimal costs determine their mandated descending order; producing and comparison-ordering those rows requires Omega(K log K) work in the general case, while the query creates each combination once and sorts the K results once.

replacement_checks.evidence: With n unique topping names the result contains exactly binom(n, 3) rows, and arbitrary costs require those rows to be returned in total-cost order.
The two strict-name joins generate each three-row combination exactly once in O(K) work, followed by one O(K log K) result sort.
Authored cases cover minimum and empty result sizes, all equal-cost ties, decimal rounding, primary-versus-secondary ordering, and complete combination cardinality.
